[
  {
    "i": 0,
    "architecture": "tandem_2T",
    "absorber": "perovskite/silicon",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 29, "unit": "%", "anchor": "When exemplarily applied to a high‐efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency PCE of 29%, the method reveals that approximately 1.9% absolute efficiency loss can be attributed to resistive effects."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "The authors extract the local tandem series resistance (LTR S) of perovskite/silicon tandem devices using bias-voltage-dependent photoluminescence imaging combined with the generalized Planck's law.", "anchor": "The method is based on bias‐voltage‐dependent photoluminescence (PL) imaging under two different illumination intensities, coupled with the generalized Planck's law.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Finite element simulations confirm the robustness of the LTR S extraction method under realistic conditions such as current mismatch and low shunt resistance.", "anchor": "Finite element simulations demonstrate the robustness of the method under a range of realistic conditions, including current mismatch, low shunt resistance, and luminescence coupling effects.", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "Applying the method to a 29% tandem device attributes about 1.9% absolute efficiency loss to resistive effects.", "anchor": "the method reveals that approximately 1.9% absolute efficiency loss can be attributed to resistive effects.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 1,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.02, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The Me4+LYS-F-based device demonstrates superior interfacial energy level alignment and reduced interface defects, ultimately achieving a power conversion efficiency of 25.02% and a high fill factor of 83.64%."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Co-assembly of the donor-acceptor SAMs LYS-H or LYS-F with Me4 improves hole extraction, wettability and perovskite crystallinity in inverted PSCs.", "anchor": "This study proposes two newly designed donor-acceptor (D-A) SAMs, LYS-H and its fluorinated derivative LYS-F, and employs a co-assembly strategy with Me4 to overcome these limitations.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The Me4+LYS-F device achieves a PCE of 25.02% with a fill factor of 83.64%.", "anchor": "The Me4+LYS-F-based device demonstrates superior interfacial energy level alignment and reduced interface defects, ultimately achieving a power conversion efficiency of 25.02% and a high fill factor of 83.64%.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Unencapsulated Me4+LYS-H and Me4+LYS-F devices show improved operational stability versus pristine Me4 in air in the dark.", "anchor": "Furthermore, both unencapsulated Me4+LYS-H and Me4+LYS-F devices demonstrate substantially improved operational stability compared to the pristine Me4 device, when measured in air (RH ≈ 30%) under dark conditions at 25 °C.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 2,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 25.54, "unit": "%", "anchor": "As a result, TPA‐CN ‐modified devices achieve a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.54%, compared to 21.80% for unmodified control devices."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": "ISOS-D-1",
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "The p-type organic dye TPA-CN is used as a SAM interlayer between NiOx and the perovskite in inverted PSCs.", "anchor": "In this study, a traditional p ‐type organic dye ( TPA‐CN ), commonly used in p ‐type NiO x dye‐sensitized solar cells, is employed as self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) molecules for interface modification between NiO x and perovskite in inverted PSCs.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "TPA-CN modification raises the peak PCE from 21.80% to 25.54%.", "anchor": "As a result, TPA‐CN ‐modified devices achieve a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.54%, compared to 21.80% for unmodified control devices.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Unencapsulated devices retain 89.2% of initial PCE after 1800 h under ISOS-D-1 and 95.3% after 500 h of 1-sun illumination.", "anchor": "Notably, unencapsulated devices maintain 89.2% of their initial PCE after 1800 h under ambient conditions (ISOS‐D‐1) and 95.3% after 500 h of continuous 1‐sun illumination.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 3,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": "Cs/FA hybrid perovskite (wide-bandgap)",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 20.3, "unit": "%", "anchor": "PSCs fabricated via sequential deposition of the inorganic scaffold demonstrate improved process repeatability and reach an efficiency of 20.3%, ranking among the highest reported efficiencies for wide‐bandgap hybrid two‐step processed PSCs."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "A fully sequential deposition route separately depositing CsCl and PbI2 is presented for hybrid two-step perovskite processing.", "anchor": "In this work, we present a fully sequential route, wherein the inorganic materials CsCl and PbI 2 are deposited separately, allowing for facile industrial implementation as compared to the commonly codeposited inorganic scaffold.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Codeposition yields horizontal PbI2 platelet growth while sequential deposition promotes vertical growth with a secondary tilted orientation.", "anchor": "Microstructural analysis reveals a change in preferred crystal orientation of the PbI 2 platelets with codeposition resulting in horizontal growth, whereas sequential deposition promotes vertical growth with a secondary tilted orientation.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Sequentially deposited PSCs reach 20.3% efficiency, among the highest for wide-bandgap hybrid two-step PSCs.", "anchor": "PSCs fabricated via sequential deposition of the inorganic scaffold demonstrate improved process repeatability and reach an efficiency of 20.3%, ranking among the highest reported efficiencies for wide‐bandgap hybrid two‐step processed PSCs.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 4,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": "CsCH(NH2)2PbI3",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 21.3, "unit": "%", "anchor": "This resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 21.3% with a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.14 V."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": "ISOS-D-2",
    "t80_h": {"value": 700, "unit": "h", "anchor": "TPA‐Py modification extended the T80 lifetime to ≈700 h compared to only 200 h for the reference under harsh heating stress in ambient conditions."},
    "claims": [
      {"text": "TPA-Py with a pyridine anchor is used for intergrain bulk modification of double-cation perovskite absorbers to enhance thermal stability.", "anchor": "In this work, a 4‐(pyridin‐4‐yl)triphenylamine (TPA‐Py) with pyridine anchor group was employed for intergrain bulk modification of double‐cation CsCH(NH 2 ) 2 PbI 3 perovskite absorbers to enhance thermal stability.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "TPA-Py devices reach 21.3% PCE with 1.14 V open-circuit voltage.", "anchor": "This resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 21.3% with a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.14 V.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "TPA-Py extends the T80 lifetime at 85 °C to about 700 h versus 200 h for the reference.", "anchor": "TPA‐Py modification extended the T80 lifetime to ≈700 h compared to only 200 h for the reference under harsh heating stress in ambient conditions.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 5,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": "PEA2Cs3Pb4I13",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 15.52, "unit": "%", "anchor": "ultimately achieving additive‐free and passivator‐free PEA 2 Cs 3 Pb 4 I 13 PSCs with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 15.52% (5.33% efficiency of PSCs in N 2 )."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Air annealing with precise humidity control yields cesium-based 2D perovskite films with regular low-n phase distribution and vertical orientation.", "anchor": "Herein, we propose an air‐annealing process coupled with a precise humidity control strategy to prepare cesium‐based 2D perovskite films featuring regular low‐ n ‐value phase distribution and vertical crystal orientation.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Additive-free PEA2Cs3Pb4I13 PSCs made by air annealing reach 15.52% PCE versus 5.33% for N2-annealed devices.", "anchor": "ultimately achieving additive‐free and passivator‐free PEA 2 Cs 3 Pb 4 I 13 PSCs with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 15.52% (5.33% efficiency of PSCs in N 2 ).", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Air-annealed devices retain 90% of initial PCE after 1300 h storage in N2 and over 80% after 1200 h of MPPT under illumination.", "anchor": "The air‐annealed devices can retain 90% of the initial PCE after 1300‐h storage in N 2 and over 80% of its initial PCE after 1200 h of continuous maximum power point tracking under illumination.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 6,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": "triple-cation perovskite (1.61 eV)",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 19.61, "unit": "%", "anchor": "This dual function yields an optimized perovskite solar cell with a champion PCE of 19.61%, demonstrating the strategy's efficacy in enhancing both film quality and device performance."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Urea is introduced as a multifunctional additive in vacuum-assisted triple-cation perovskite solar cells with a 1.61 eV bandgap.", "anchor": "In this study, we introduce urea as a multifunctional additive to fabricate triple‐cation perovskite solar cells with a bandgap of 1.61 eV.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Urea coordination via amino and carbonyl groups slows crystallization kinetics during vacuum-assisted deposition.", "anchor": "Incorporating urea into the precursor solution enhances coordination between its amino and carbonyl groups and the perovskite components, effectively slowing the crystallization kinetics during vacuum‐assisted deposition.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The optimized urea-treated triple-cation device achieves a champion PCE of 19.61%.", "anchor": "This dual function yields an optimized perovskite solar cell with a champion PCE of 19.61%, demonstrating the strategy's efficacy in enhancing both film quality and device performance.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 7,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": {"value": 22.14, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The PCE of PSCs (ITO/SnO 2 /perovskite/Spiro‐OMETAD/Ag) is increased from 20.16% to 22.14%, demonstrating the universality of this doping method."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Ribavirin doping raises Voc from 1.077 to 1.151 V and PCE from 17.05% to 19.86% in inverted PSCs.", "anchor": "This increases the open‐circuit voltage of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) (ITO/PEDOT:PSS/perovskite/PCBM/BCP/Ag) from 1.077 to 1.151 V, and the power conversion efficiency (PCE) increases significantly from 17.05% to 19.86%.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "DFT calculations show ribavirin improves defect formation energies of VI, VMA, VPb and PbI.", "anchor": "Based on density functional theory calculations, the defect formation energies of V I , V MA , V Pb , and Pb I in perovskite are improved.", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "After about 900 h of ambient storage, ribavirin devices retain 84.33% of initial PCE versus 13.44% for controls.", "anchor": "After ≈900 h of storage, the PCE of the ribavirin‐based device retains 84.33% of its initial PCE, while the control‐based device retains only 13.44% of its initial PCE.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 8,
    "architecture": "p-i-n",
    "absorber": "2D/3D perovskite (oleylammonium, 1.55 eV)",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.22, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The fabricated inverted PSCs with 1.55 eV bandgap achieved a maximum PCE of 26.22% for small area and 24.6% for 1cm 2 devices, as well as 21.1% for mini-modules (6.8 cm 2 )."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": {"value": 1, "unit": "cm^2", "anchor": "The fabricated inverted PSCs with 1.55 eV bandgap achieved a maximum PCE of 26.22% for small area and 24.6% for 1cm 2 devices, as well as 21.1% for mini-modules (6.8 cm 2 )."},
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "Incorporating long-chain oleylammonium ligands into the perovskite ink forms 2D perovskite with dimensionality n ≥ 3 in a one-step process.", "anchor": "Here, we propose an in situ fabrication method incorporating long-chain oleylammonium (OlyA + ) ligands directly into the perovskite ink.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The resulting inverted PSCs achieve 26.22% small-area, 24.6% for 1 cm2, and 21.1% for 6.8 cm2 mini-module PCEs.", "anchor": "The fabricated inverted PSCs with 1.55 eV bandgap achieved a maximum PCE of 26.22% for small area and 24.6% for 1cm 2 devices, as well as 21.1% for mini-modules (6.8 cm 2 ).", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "Devices with the in situ 2D/3D heterojunction retain 90% of initial PCE after 1200 h photothermal stability and 80% after 1050 h outdoor testing.", "anchor": "Additionally, the PSCs with in situ formed 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions retained 90% and 80% of their initial PCE after 1200 h photothermal stability and 1050 h outdoor testing, respectively.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 9,
    "architecture": "unknown",
    "absorber": "FAPbI3",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 26.13, "unit": "%", "anchor": "The ZL1-modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 26.13%, significantly outperforming the control device (24.20%)."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "The multidentate additive ZL1 stabilizes the α-FAPbI3 phase through synergistic multisite interactions suppressing FA loss.", "anchor": "Herein, we designed and synthesized a novel multifunctional additive (ZL1) to stabilize α -FAPbI 3 perovskite phase through synergistic multisite interactions:", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "ZL1-modified devices reach 26.13% PCE versus 24.20% for the control.", "anchor": "The ZL1-modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 26.13%, significantly outperforming the control device (24.20%).", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "ZL1 treatment also raises wide-bandgap PSC efficiency from 18.44% to 20.53%.", "anchor": "A similar improvement is observed in wide-bandgap PSCs, with efficiency increasing from 18.44% to 20.53% after ZL1 treatment.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 10,
    "architecture": "none",
    "absorber": null,
    "pce_champion": null,
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": {"value": 21.56, "unit": "%", "anchor": "Consequently, the optimized p-MPSCs exhibit an average open-circuit voltage enhancement of over 50 mV, a steady-state power conversion efficiency of 21.56% and operational stability exceeding 1500 h at 55 °C under simulated 1-sun illumination using a halogen lamp without a UV filter."},
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "A strong electron-withdrawing polymer spontaneously forms a negative gradient distribution within the mesoporous scaffold during fabrication of p-MPSCs.", "anchor": "Owing to its large molecular size, this polymer spontaneously forms a negative gradient distribution from top to bottom within the mesoporous scaffold during fabrication.", "evidence_type": "measurement"},
      {"text": "The gradient p-doping profile enabling better hole transport is corroborated by device simulation and cross-sectional photoluminescence mapping.", "anchor": "This distribution creates a favorable gradient p-doping profile within p-MPSCs, which facilitates more efficient hole transport, a finding corroborated by combined device simulation and cross-sectional photoluminescence mapping.", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "Optimized p-MPSCs show over 50 mV Voc enhancement, a steady-state PCE of 21.56%, and stability exceeding 1500 h at 55 °C under 1-sun illumination.", "anchor": "Consequently, the optimized p-MPSCs exhibit an average open-circuit voltage enhancement of over 50 mV, a steady-state power conversion efficiency of 21.56% and operational stability exceeding 1500 h at 55 °C under simulated 1-sun illumination using a halogen lamp without a UV filter.", "evidence_type": "measurement"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "i": 11,
    "architecture": "n-i-p",
    "absorber": "FA0.75MA0.25Sn0.95Ge0.05I3/FA0.75Cs0.25SnI3",
    "pce_champion": {"value": 32.39, "unit": "%", "anchor": "This device with optimized parameters showed a PCE of 32.39 %, a short circuit current density (J SC ) of 35.31 mA/cm 2 , an open circuit voltage (V OC ) of 1.05 V and a fill factor (FF) of 87.68 % at 300 K."},
    "pce_certified": null,
    "pce_stabilised": null,
    "active_area_cm2": null,
    "stability_protocol": null,
    "t80_h": null,
    "claims": [
      {"text": "SCAPS-1D simulation optimizes lead-free mixed-cation Sn-based heterojunction PSCs with dual FA0.75MA0.25Sn0.95Ge0.05I3/FA0.75Cs0.25SnI3 absorbers.", "anchor": "This simulation study analyzes and optimizes lead-free mixed cation Sn-based heterojunction perovskite solar cells (HPSCs) with dual (FA 0.75 MA 0.25 Sn 0.95 Ge 0.05 I 3 /FA 0.75 Cs 0.25 SnI 3 ) absorber layers to maximize the overall power conversion efficiency (PCE) using the one-dimensional solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D).", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "Among ETLs compared, ZnOS gives the highest efficiency of 26.53%.", "anchor": "At optimal levels, the ETL ZnOS achieved 26.53 % efficiency, surpassing other ETLs such as TiO₂ (26.48 %), WS₂ (25.86 %), C 60 (24.55 %) and PCBM (21.22 %).", "evidence_type": "simulation"},
      {"text": "The optimized FTO/ZnOS/dual-absorber/CuI/Ni device shows a simulated PCE of 32.39% with FF of 87.68% at 300 K.", "anchor": "This device with optimized parameters showed a PCE of 32.39 %, a short circuit current density (J SC ) of 35.31 mA/cm 2 , an open circuit voltage (V OC ) of 1.05 V and a fill factor (FF) of 87.68 % at 300 K.", "evidence_type": "simulation"}
    ]
  }
]
